checklist.step: Build and maintain the inventory of vendors touching FCIC Protected Information
actions: In Coupa/Ariba run the active-supplier report filtered to the crop line cost centers and export supplier name, category and spend.
Cross-check against the CMDB application-to-vendor mappings so IT hosting and data processors with system access are captured, not just spend vendors.
Ask each crop business owner (Claims Director / Manager, UW Operations Manager) to confirm any loss adjusters, MGAs or print/mail vendors missing from the extract.
Record for each vendor: services performed, whether it receives Protected Information or PII, and the systems it touches; file the inventory in the vendor register.
checklist.done: a dated vendor inventory exists covering spend, IT and delivery vendors, each flagged for Protected Information access.

checklist.step: Classify each vendor's data access and FCIP delivery role
actions: In Archer open the third-party module and create/update an engagement record per vendor from the inventory.
Set the data classification: Protected Information (policyholder SSN/EIN, APH yield data, claim records) vs PII-only vs no regulated data, citing the Appendix III definition.
Tag delivery-function vendors (loss adjustment, agency/MGA, sales closing/reporting support) — these carry SRA Section IV obligations beyond data security.
Assign the inherent risk tier that drives assessment depth and contract clause set.
checklist.done: every inventoried vendor has an Archer record with a data classification, delivery-role tag and risk tier.

checklist.step: Maintain the SRA mandatory-clause library
actions: In Icertis open Clause Library ▸ FCIP/SRA set and confirm one clause exists for each mandatory term: one-hour incident reporting flow-down per Appendix III, FISMA-consistent security controls per SRA Section IV(a)(4), USDA/RMA/OIG/GAO audit and records access, FCIP-only data-use restriction, conflict-of-interest and standards-of-conduct per Section IV(d), LASH/Manual 14 compliance for loss adjustment services, and records retention of 3 years after the reinsurance year.
On each annual SRA reissue (effective July 1), redline the library against the new SRA text and Appendix III within 45 days.
Version-stamp each clause with the SRA year it implements and retire superseded versions.
Notify the Contracts Manager which live agreements carry a retired clause version and need amendment at next renewal.
checklist.done: the clause library carries a current-SRA-year version of every mandatory clause and a list of agreements on stale versions.

checklist.step: Draft the vendor/data-sharing agreement from the FCIP template
actions: In Icertis create the agreement from the FCIP vendor template matching the vendor's classification (data processor, loss adjustment, MGA/agency).
Auto-insert the mandatory clause set for that classification and confirm none were dropped by the template rules.
Complete the data-sharing exhibit: data elements shared, transfer channel, storage location (US-only per FISMA expectations), permitted subprocessors and return/destruction terms.
Route the draft to Privacy Counsel and the Third-Party Risk Manager as parallel reviewers in the Icertis workflow.
checklist.done: a draft agreement with the full mandatory clause set and completed data exhibit is in review workflow.

checklist.step: Complete the privacy review of the data-sharing terms
actions: Check the data exhibit lists only elements the vendor needs for the contracted FCIP function, and that use is contractually limited to FCIP delivery per the SRA data-use restriction.

Confirm the one-hour Appendix III incident flow-down obligates the vendor to notify the Company immediately on discovery of any loss or unauthorized disclosure, suspected or confirmed, so the Company can meet its own one-hour clock to FCIC.
Verify individual-notification and cost-allocation terms for breaches originating at the vendor.
Record the review outcome and any required redlines in the Icertis workflow step.
checklist.done: privacy review is recorded as passed, or redlines are issued, inside the agreement workflow.

checklist.step: Assess the vendor's security controls before granting data access
actions: Issue the security questionnaire mapped to NIST SP 800-53 moderate-baseline families from Archer and collect the vendor's SOC 2 Type II or equivalent audit report.
Have the Security GRC Analyst score the responses and log findings as Archer issues with owners and due dates.
For vendors hosting Protected Information, confirm encryption at rest and in transit, US data residency and background-check practices consistent with FISMA expectations.
Block contract execution in the workflow until high-risk findings carry an accepted remediation plan.
checklist.done: the Archer assessment is complete and no unmitigated high-risk finding stands against a data-hosting vendor.

checklist.step: Verify loss-adjustment vendors meet LASH and Manual 14 standards
actions: For each loss adjustment firm, collect the adjuster roster with RMA proficiency-program status and continuing-education records required by Manual 14 and the Loss Adjustment Standards Handbook (LASH).
Confirm the agreement obligates the vendor to use only adjusters meeting FCIC proficiency standards and to follow LASH procedures on every FCIP claim.
Spot-check three roster names against training certificates supplied by the vendor.
File the roster and certificates with the agreement record.
checklist.done: each loss-adjustment vendor's agreement carries the LASH/proficiency obligation and a verified adjuster roster is on file.

checklist.step: Determine whether the vendor must be disclosed in the Plan of Operations
actions: Test the vendor against the SRA Plan of Operations disclosure triggers: MGAs, affiliates performing delivery functions, and material subcontracts for policyholder service, loss adjustment or data processing.
Record the determination and its SRA cite on the agreement record.
Add triggered vendors to the Plan of Operations subcontractor listing maintained for the April 1 submission to RMA.
Where a material arrangement begins mid-year, ask the Regulatory Affairs Manager whether an interim notification to RMA is required rather than waiting for April 1.
checklist.done: every vendor has a documented disclosure determination and triggered vendors sit on the April 1 listing.

checklist.step: Negotiate redlines without surrendering mandatory clauses
actions: Run negotiations through Icertis redline tracking so every clause deviation is visible against the library version.
Treat the mandatory SRA clause set as non-negotiable; a vendor refusing the one-hour flow-down or USDA audit rights cannot receive Protected Information.
Escalate any requested deviation to Legal Counsel with the vendor's rationale; only Legal Counsel may grant a documented waiver, and never on Appendix III terms.
Log the final negotiated position per clause in the agreement record.
checklist.done: the final draft retains every mandatory clause or carries a Legal Counsel waiver on non-Appendix-III terms only.

checklist.step: Execute the agreement before any data flows
actions: Send the final agreement for signature via DocuSign to the vendor signatory and the Company signer per the delegation-of-authority matrix.
Confirm both signatures and the effective date land before the planned first data transfer or system access date.
File the completed DocuSign certificate of completion with the executed agreement in Icertis.
Notify the Vendor Manager that execution is complete so onboarding can proceed.
checklist.done: a fully executed agreement with signature certificate exists and pre-dates first data access.

checklist.step: Register the executed agreement with clause metadata
actions: File the executed agreement in the CLM repository indexed by vendor, service type, effective/expiry dates and reinsurance year.
Complete the clause-matrix metadata: mark each mandatory SRA clause present/waived with the library version used.
Set the renewal workflow with T-90/T-60/T-30 alerts to the Contracts Manager.
Link the Archer engagement record and the Plan of Operations disclosure determination to the contract record.
checklist.done: the repository shows the agreement with complete clause metadata, linked risk record and armed renewal alerts.

checklist.step: Onboard the vendor with least-privilege access and an approved transfer channel
actions: Request vendor accounts through the IAM platform limited to the systems and data named in the data exhibit; the Access Management Analyst provisions against that exhibit, nothing broader.
Stand up the agreed transfer channel (SFTP with encryption or API) and prohibit ad-hoc email of Protected Information in the onboarding instructions.
Deliver the Company's incident-reporting contact card so the vendor can hit the one-hour flow-down clock.
Confirm with the Chief Info Security Officer's team that DLP monitoring covers the new channel.
checklist.done: vendor access matches the data exhibit, the transfer channel is live and monitored, and incident contacts are delivered.

checklist.step: Compile and submit the subcontractor disclosures in the Plan of Operations by April 1
actions: By February 1, extract from the CLM repository all vendors flagged for Plan of Operations disclosure, with services, territories and contract terms.
Draft the subcontractor/MGA exhibit of the Plan of Operations and reconcile it to the vendor inventory so no disclosable arrangement is omitted.
Hand the exhibit to the Regulatory Affairs Manager for inclusion in the Plan of Operations submitted to RMA by April 1 for the coming reinsurance year.
File RMA's acknowledgement or approval correspondence with the exhibit in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the April 1 Plan of Operations carries a reconciled subcontractor exhibit and RMA's response is filed.

checklist.step: Re-certify vendor compliance annually and amend stale agreements
actions: Each reinsurance year, send data-access vendors a compliance certification covering clause adherence, subcontractor changes and security posture, and chase non-responders at 15 and 30 days.
Trigger Archer reassessment for vendors whose services or data scope changed.
Amend agreements carrying retired clause versions at renewal, prioritizing any Appendix III change within 45 days of the SRA reissue.
Report certification status and open amendments to the Head of Compliance quarterly.
checklist.done: every data-access vendor holds a current-year certification and no agreement carries a stale Appendix III clause.

checklist.step: Log and remediate agreement exceptions
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any vendor found receiving Protected Information without an executed agreement or with a missing mandatory clause.
Decide with the Chief Info Security Officer whether data access is suspended pending remediation; record the decision and rationale.
Assign root cause (missed intake, expired agreement, scope creep), an owner and a remediation date; Legal Counsel signs off closure.
Feed every exception into the annual verification test as a mandatory retest row.
checklist.done: every exception has an issue, an access decision, a root cause, an owner and a signed closure.

testing.step: Build the vendor population from spend, systems and delivery records
actions: Extract active crop-line suppliers with payments in the reinsurance year from Coupa/Ariba.
Union in vendors with system access from the CMDB and IAM vendor-account listings so no-spend data processors surface.
Add loss-adjustment firms from the claims assignment records supplied by the Claims Director / Manager.
Reconcile the combined list to the Archer vendor inventory and resolve differences before sampling.
testing.done: a reconciled population of data-access and delivery vendors is documented with sources.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to executed agreements in the CLM repository
actions: Match every population vendor to an executed, in-force agreement record.
Check the agreement effective date pre-dates the vendor's first data access or first claim assignment.
List unmatched vendors and post-access executions as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every vendor maps to a pre-dated executed agreement or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the method
actions: Take 100% of loss-adjustment firms, MGAs and vendors hosting Protected Information.
Randomly select 15 additional vendors (seeded, reproducible) from the remainder, minimum 25 in total.
Record seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers all high-risk vendor classes at 100%.

testing.step: Re-perform the mandatory-clause check against the current SRA
actions: Read each sampled executed agreement against the current SRA Sections IV(a)(4), IV(d), IV(f) and Appendix III text pulled from the RMA website, not against the Company's clause matrix.

Confirm the one-hour incident flow-down, FISMA-consistent controls, USDA/OIG/GAO audit rights, FCIP-only data use, conflict-of-interest terms and 3-year records retention are each present and unweakened.
Treat a Legal Counsel waiver on any Appendix III term as a fail; verify other waivers carry dated counsel sign-off.
Capture the clause page references into the workpaper per vendor.
testing.done: each sampled agreement has an independent clause-by-clause result traced to current SRA text.

testing.step: Verify privacy and security reviews pre-date execution
actions: Open the Archer engagement record for each sampled vendor and read the assessment completion date and residual-risk outcome.
Confirm the privacy review step in the Icertis workflow closed before the DocuSign execution date.
Flag any vendor executed with an open high-risk finding and no accepted remediation plan.
testing.done: every sampled execution is preceded by completed privacy and security reviews or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Trace disclosable vendors to the April 1 Plan of Operations
actions: Re-perform the disclosure determination for each sampled vendor against the SRA Plan of Operations triggers.
Trace each triggered vendor to the subcontractor/MGA exhibit actually submitted to RMA, and check the submission date met April 1.
Verify RMA's acknowledgement correspondence is filed in the compliance evidence repository.
List any disclosable vendor absent from the filed exhibit as an exception.
testing.done: every disclosable sampled vendor appears in the timely filed Plan of Operations exhibit.

testing.step: Verify loss-adjuster proficiency evidence
actions: For each sampled loss-adjustment firm, pull the adjuster roster and training certificates filed with the agreement.
Select three adjusters per firm and trace their names to FCIP claims they worked in the claims platform, confirming proficiency status was current at the adjustment date.
Flag any adjuster working claims without current Manual 14/LASH proficiency evidence.
testing.done: sampled adjusters trace to current proficiency evidence at the dates they adjusted FCIP claims.

testing.step: Recompute agreement currency and access alignment
actions: Recompute each sampled agreement's expiry against today and against the vendor's last data-transfer or system-access date from IAM logs.
Flag any lapsed agreement with continuing data flows as a reportable breach, not a documentation gap.
Compare provisioned vendor access against the data exhibit and note any access broader than contracted.
testing.done: no sampled vendor shows data flows after expiry or access beyond the contracted exhibit, or breaches are logged.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with vendor, defect, and compliance impact under the SRA.
Assign root cause (intake miss, stale clause library, waived mandatory term, lapsed renewal) and an accountable owner.
Set remediation dates; for lapsed-agreement data flows, trigger the access-suspension decision with the Chief Info Security Officer.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold and state the conclusion: effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective.
Have the independent reviewer — who negotiated or approved none of the sampled agreements — sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Head of Compliance and General Counsel ahead of the April 1 Plan of Operations, and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed before the April 1 submission.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per initiative — PIA must close before go-live; supporting security assessments must be producible to FCIC on request under Section IV(a)(4), targeted within 45 days of an FCIC ask

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC platform SLAs on each open PIA (screening 5 business days, full assessment 20 business days) with escalation to the Data Protection Officer at breach; project gates block go-live on open PIAs

checklist.step: Screen every new initiative for Protected Information processing at intake
actions: Embed a privacy screening questionnaire as a mandatory gate in the PPM intake so no crop-line project passes stage 1 without it.
Have the Project Manager answer: data elements processed (SSN/EIN, APH yields, claim files, geospatial farm data), volumes, new vendors, cross-border storage, and automated decisioning.
Auto-create a GRC screening record from the questionnaire and route it to the privacy team queue.
Return a screening verdict within 5 business days: no privacy impact, standard controls apply, or full PIA required.
checklist.done: every intake carries a screening record and verdict issued within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Classify which initiatives are high-risk and need a full PIA
actions: Apply the high-risk triggers from the PIA procedure: new repository of Protected Information, analytics or ML scoring on policyholder data, cloud or vendor hosting change, matching against external datasets (FSA/acreage data), or large-scale claims imagery collection.
Record the trigger(s) met on the GRC record with the Appendix III data classes involved.
For borderline calls, take the decision to the Privacy Officer and minute the rationale.
Set the PIA due date ahead of the project's go-live milestone in the PPM tool.
checklist.done: each screened initiative carries a documented high-risk determination with triggers and a PIA due date.

checklist.step: Categorize the system under FIPS 199 and set the control baseline
actions: Rate confidentiality, integrity and availability impact for the information types (policyholder PII, premium/claim financials) using FIPS 199 levels; FCIP Protected Information defaults to at least Moderate confidentiality.
Derive the NIST SP 800-53 baseline (Moderate) and record tailoring decisions with justification.
Enter the categorization on the GRC record so the control mapping step inherits it.
Have the IT Security Manager countersign the categorization.
checklist.done: a countersigned FIPS 199 categorization and SP 800-53 baseline sit on the GRC record.

checklist.step: Document the data flows and minimization decisions
actions: Draw the end-to-end flow: sources (policy admin, claims platform, RMA-provided data), processing steps, storage locations, recipients and retention points.
Challenge each data element with the Business Analyst: is SSN/EIN needed, or does the policy number suffice; strike elements without a documented need.
Record retention per node against the 3-years-after-reinsurance-year rule and the destruction method.
Attach the flow diagram to the PIA record.
checklist.done: the PIA carries a complete data-flow diagram with per-element necessity and retention decisions.

checklist.step: Assess risks and map SP 800-53 controls to each
actions: Score likelihood and impact for each identified risk (unauthorized disclosure, re-identification from yield/geospatial data, vendor compromise, excessive retention) on the GRC 5x5 scale.

Map the mitigating SP 800-53 controls (AC access enforcement, SC-28 encryption at rest, AU audit logging, IR incident response hooks to the one-hour Appendix III clock) and record implementation status per control.
Raise remediation actions with owners and dates for every control gap.
Compute the residual risk rating the DPO will be asked to accept.
checklist.done: every risk maps to controls with status, gaps carry owned actions, and a residual rating is computed.

checklist.step: Review vendor and cross-border hosting arrangements inside the PIA
actions: Where the initiative uses a vendor, confirm an executed data-sharing agreement with the mandatory SRA clause set exists (coordinate with the Contracts Manager) before the PIA can close.
Verify hosting keeps Protected Information in US regions consistent with FISMA expectations, and document any exception for DPO decision.
Check subprocessor chains are disclosed and contractually bound to the same flow-downs.
Record the legal review outcome on the PIA record.
checklist.done: the PIA records a legal review confirming contracts and residency, or an escalated exception.

checklist.step: Obtain residual-risk acceptance and close the PIA before go-live
actions: Review the completed assessment, challenge low-balled likelihood scores, and either accept the residual risk or return the PIA with required mitigations.
Record the acceptance decision, date and conditions on the GRC record; conditions become tracked actions.
Confirm the PPM go-live gate reads the PIA status — the Release Coordinator may not ship while the PIA is open.
Notify the Privacy Officer and Project Manager of closure.
checklist.done: a dated DPO acceptance closes the PIA and the go-live gate shows green only after closure.

checklist.step: Wire PIA outputs into the security monitoring stack
actions: Onboard the new system's audit logs into Splunk with alerting on bulk Protected Information export and privileged access anomalies.
Register the system in the CMDB with its FIPS 199 rating so vulnerability scanning (Qualys/Tenable) prioritizes it.
Confirm incident-response runbooks reference the system so any breach feeds the one-hour FCIC clock under Appendix III.
Evidence the onboarding with a screenshot of the Splunk index and alert rules filed to the PIA record.
checklist.done: the system logs to the SIEM with export alerts, is CMDB-registered, and IR runbooks reference it.

checklist.step: Maintain the ongoing risk-based security process over live processing
actions: Run the continuous-monitoring calendar: quarterly vulnerability scan review, annual control self-assessment against the SP 800-53 baseline, and annual penetration test for internet-facing Protected Information systems.
Log control failures as GRC issues with owners and dates; re-open the PIA where the risk profile materially changes.
Summarize posture to the Chief Info Security Officer quarterly, satisfying the SRA's ongoing risk-based security process expectation.
File each cycle's artifacts to the system's GRC record.
checklist.done: the monitoring calendar shows completed cycles with filed artifacts and tracked issues.

checklist.step: Trigger PIA refresh on material change
actions: Subscribe the privacy team to the change-management workflow so changes tagged to Protected Information systems route a change-screening task.
Re-screen on triggers: new data elements, new vendor, new use (e.g. training an ML model on claims data), or architecture change.
Version the PIA — never overwrite — so FCIC can see the assessment as it stood at any date.
Record 'no refresh needed' decisions with rationale rather than leaving them silent.
checklist.done: material changes route to re-screening and every decision, including no-refresh, is recorded and versioned.

checklist.step: Keep the internal and external IT security audit set FCIC-ready
actions: Maintain an index of internal IT audits, external assessments (SOC 2, penetration tests) and the annual FISMA-aligned self-assessment covering Protected Information systems.
Store final reports in the compliance evidence repository with redaction-ready copies, since SRA Section IV(a)(4) makes them available to FCIC on request.
Rehearse the production package annually: confirm the index retrieves every report within 2 business days.
Log any FCIC or RMA request and its fulfillment date against the 45-day response target.
checklist.done: an indexed, retrievable audit set exists and any FCIC request is logged with its fulfillment date.

checklist.step: Maintain the PIA register as the single record of assessments
actions: Keep one register row per PIA: initiative, systems, data classes, high-risk triggers, completion date, DPO acceptance date, go-live date and refresh history.
Reconcile the register quarterly against PPM go-lives touching Protected Information to catch initiatives that bypassed intake.
Report bypasses immediately to the Privacy Officer as exceptions, not register updates.
Export the register quarterly to the compliance evidence repository as the FCIC-ready snapshot.
checklist.done: the register reconciles to go-lives quarterly and snapshots are filed.

checklist.step: Train PIA reviewers and project intake staff
actions: Assign the PIA procedure module in Cornerstone to privacy staff, Security GRC Analysts and PPM intake coordinators annually.
Include Appendix III data classes and the one-hour incident linkage so reviewers recognize FCIC-specific stakes.
Track completion and chase past-due assignees at 15 days; report completion to the Privacy Officer.
File the completion report with the annual training evidence.
checklist.done: all reviewer and intake staff show current-year completion in the LMS.

checklist.step: Report PIA program status to governance
actions: Present quarterly to the privacy/security governance committee: PIAs opened/closed, aging against SLA, residual-risk acceptances, bypass exceptions and FCIC requests received.
Escalate any initiative live without a PIA for a stop/continue decision minuted by the committee.
Minute decisions and file the deck and minutes in the compliance evidence repository.
Feed systemic findings back into the PIA procedure's annual review.
checklist.done: quarterly minutes show status, escalations decided, and filed materials.

checklist.step: Log and remediate PIA exceptions
actions: Raise a GRC issue for every high-risk go-live without a completed PIA, with the data classes exposed and the period of unassessed processing.
Obtain a stop/continue decision from the DPO and Chief Info Security Officer within 3 business days of discovery.
Run the retrospective PIA, assign root cause (intake bypass, mis-screening, gate override) and an owner.
Close only on DPO sign-off and carry the exception into the annual verification test.
checklist.done: every exception has a decision within 3 business days, a retrospective PIA, root cause, owner and DPO-signed closure.

testing.step: Build the population of go-lives that touched Protected Information
actions: Extract all initiatives and material changes that went live in the reinsurance year from the PPM tool and the change-management records — deliberately not from the PIA register.
Filter to those touching crop-line systems holding Protected Information using the CMDB data classifications.
Reconcile the count against release records supplied by the Release Coordinator and resolve differences before sampling.
testing.done: an independently built, reconciled population of Protected Information go-lives exists.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the PIA register
actions: Match each population row to a PIA register row; list unmatched go-lives as automatic exceptions.
Check the DPO acceptance date pre-dates the go-live date on every match.
Note screening verdicts of 'no privacy impact' for re-performance rather than accepting them.
testing.done: every go-live matches a pre-dated PIA or acceptance, or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the method
actions: Take 100% of AI/analytics initiatives, cloud migrations and new vendor-hosted repositories.
Randomly select 10 further rows (seeded, reproducible) from the remainder, minimum 20 rows total.
Record seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all highest-risk classes at 100%.

testing.step: Re-perform the high-risk screening on sampled rows
actions: Read each sampled initiative's scope documents and reach an independent full-PIA-required verdict before looking at the recorded screening.
Compare to the recorded verdict; any initiative screened out that meets a high-risk trigger is an exception.
Pay specific attention to ML models trained on claims or yield data — the most commonly under-screened class.
testing.done: each sampled row carries an independent screening conclusion compared against the record.

testing.step: Verify FIPS 199 categorization and control mapping quality
actions: Open each sampled PIA in the GRC platform and re-derive the FIPS 199 rating from the information types; Protected Information below Moderate confidentiality is an exception.
Check every identified risk maps to named SP 800-53 controls with an implementation status, and that gaps carried owned remediation actions.
Verify the IT Security Manager countersignature and DPO acceptance are dated and by segregated individuals.
testing.done: sampled PIAs show defensible categorizations, complete control mappings and segregated sign-offs.

testing.step: Trace technical controls into the live environment
actions: For 5 sampled systems, confirm in Splunk that audit logs are flowing and the bulk-export alert rules named in the PIA exist and have fired test events.
Confirm CMDB registration with the FIPS rating and inclusion in the Qualys/Tenable scan scope.
Ask the SOC Analyst to evidence one triaged alert from each system where available.
testing.done: sampled systems demonstrably log, alert and sit in scan scope as their PIAs claim.

testing.step: Verify the ongoing risk-based monitoring cycles ran
actions: For each sampled system, pull the continuous-monitoring artifacts: quarterly vulnerability reviews, the annual control self-assessment, and the penetration test where required.
Check cycle dates against the calendar and that failures became tracked GRC issues.
A missed annual cycle on a Protected Information system is an exception against the SRA's ongoing-process requirement.
testing.done: monitoring artifacts exist on schedule for every sampled system or misses are logged.

testing.step: Test FCIC-readiness of the audit production package
actions: Request three named audit reports (one internal, one external, one self-assessment) via the index and time the retrieval against the 2-business-day standard.
Verify any actual FCIC/RMA requests in the period were fulfilled within the 45-day target, tracing dates in the request log.
Check report versions match the final signed issues, not drafts.
testing.done: the package retrieves on time and any real requests met the 45-day target.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one GRC issue per exception stating the initiative, defect and exposure window of unassessed Protected Information processing.
Assign root cause (intake bypass, mis-screening, gate override, monitoring lapse) and an accountable owner with a date.
For go-lives without PIAs, confirm the stop/continue decision was taken and the retrospective PIA is underway.
Carry open items into next year's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance and documentation-quality thresholds and state the conclusion: effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective.
Have the independent reviewer — who performed or approved none of the sampled PIAs — sign the workpaper.
Report to the Data Protection Officer and Chief Info Security Officer and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the one-hour FCIC breach-reporting clock under SRA Appendix III; the Privacy Officer co-owns individual and state notifications

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 2026 SRA Appendix III incident-reporting terms requiring report to FCIC within one hour of discovery of any loss or unauthorized disclosure of Protected Information or PII, suspected or confirmed, re-read at each SRA reissue

In-scope processes.value: Security incident detection, triage and escalation across every system and vendor holding FCIP Protected Information — SOC monitoring, employee reports, vendor flow-down notifications and physical-loss reports (laptops, claim files)

In-scope systems.value: Detection in Splunk/SIEM, case management in the SOAR and security ticketing; the incident record carries the one-hour clock timestamps

Compliance procedure documented.value: FCIC Incident Reporting Runbook — Appendix III definitions, the one-hour clock starting at discovery not confirmation, the RMA reporting channel and contact list, the no-distinction rule for suspected incidents, and follow-up written report steps

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Info Security Officer and General Counsel; tabletop-tested twice yearly and refreshed within 45 days of any Appendix III change

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: One hour from discovery to FCIC for every incident touching Protected Information/PII; state breach statutes and individual notifications tracked per event (typically 30-60 days by state); vendor flow-downs require immediate notice to the Company

Deadline reminders configured.value: SOAR playbook auto-starts a one-hour countdown timer on any case tagged FCIP-data and pages the Incident Response Lead and Privacy Officer simultaneously; unacknowledged pages escalate to the CISO at 15 minutes

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Incident records, FCIC report copies, timestamps, forensic reports and notification letters retained 3 years after the applicable reinsurance year in the security case system and compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any report to FCIC made after the one-hour mark, or any qualifying incident not reported, is logged as a compliance exception with minute-level timeline, root cause and disposition — never quietly closed as an IT ticket

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Privacy Officer signs closure of every reportable incident after confirming FCIC, state and individual notification duties were met

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All security and privacy incidents in the reinsurance year touching systems or vendors classified as holding Protected Information, drawn from SIEM cases, the security ticket queue, the DLP alert log and vendor notifications — not just incidents already tagged FCIP

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on the one-hour clock — any qualifying incident reported late or not at all is a fail; any suspected incident held back pending confirmation is a fail of the no-distinction rule

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven; test runs semi-annually over the trailing period plus one unannounced tabletop drill measuring simulated time-to-report

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have handled any sampled incident or sit in the SOC reporting line

Evidence location for test results.value: Semi-annual incident-reporting test workpaper (population, timeline reconstructions, drill results, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-incident package: detection artifact, discovery timestamp, FCIC report copy with send time, follow-up report, forensic summary and notification letters — assembled to answer an RMA inquiry within 45 days

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Info Security Officer makes the one-hour report through the RMA-designated channel; follow-up correspondence routes through the Privacy Officer with Legal Counsel clearance

checklist.step: Maintain the FCIC incident-reporting runbook and contact chain
actions: Keep the runbook's Appendix III section current: what counts as Protected Information/PII, that the clock starts at discovery, and that suspected incidents are reported identically to confirmed ones.
Verify the RMA/FCIC reporting channel and named contacts quarterly by checking the current SRA appendix and RMA correspondence, and correct the contact card on any change.
Publish the one-page reporting card (who calls, what to say, what not to speculate on) to the SOC, service desk and claims leadership.
Version the runbook and file each version in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the runbook and contact card reflect the current SRA appendix and were verified within the last quarter.

checklist.step: Tag every FCIP data-bearing system and vendor so detection can classify instantly
actions: Flag each CMDB configuration item that stores or processes Protected Information with an 'FCIP-data' attribute, sourced from the PIA register and data classifications.
Mirror the flag into the SIEM asset model so alerts on those systems auto-tag FCIP-data.
Maintain the equivalent vendor list so a vendor's breach notice is recognized as FCIP-relevant at intake.
Reconcile the flags quarterly against the PIA register and fix drift.
checklist.done: every Protected Information system and vendor carries the FCIP-data flag in CMDB and SIEM, reconciled quarterly.

checklist.step: Auto-start the one-hour clock on qualifying alerts
actions: In the SOAR, open the FCIP incident playbook so any case created on an FCIP-data asset auto-stamps the discovery time and starts a 60-minute countdown.
Page the Incident Response Lead and Privacy Officer on playbook start; escalate to the Chief Info Security Officer if unacknowledged at 15 minutes.
Record in the case the alert source, affected asset, suspected data classes and whether exposure is loss, theft or unauthorized disclosure.
Never pause the countdown to 'confirm first' — the runbook's no-distinction rule governs.
checklist.done: qualifying cases show an auto-stamped discovery time, a running countdown and paged responders.

checklist.step: Route human-reported and physical-loss incidents into the same clock
actions: In ServiceNow, use the 'Lost device / data exposure' catalog item that forces the reporter to state whether crop policyholder data could be involved.
On a yes or unsure answer, the workflow auto-creates the SOAR case with discovery time = report time and pages the Incident Response Lead.
Capture the device or file details: laptop asset tag and encryption status, or the claim-file identifiers for paper losses reported by field staff.
Train the desk to treat 'unsure' as 'yes' — misrouting to a plain IT ticket is itself an exception.
checklist.done: human and physical reports create clocked SOAR cases at report time, with device or file identifiers captured.

checklist.step: Make the one-hour report to FCIC
actions: Within 60 minutes of the discovery stamp, report through the RMA-designated channel on the contact card, stating: reporting company and AIP code, discovery date/time, nature of the loss or disclosure, data classes suspected, systems or vendors involved, and interim containment.
State explicitly that facts are preliminary and the incident may be suspected rather than confirmed — Appendix III requires the report anyway.
Record the send time, channel, recipient and content copy in the SOAR case the moment the report goes out.
If the CISO is unreachable, the Incident Response Lead reports — the clock never waits for seniority.
checklist.done: the FCIC report is sent inside 60 minutes with send time and content evidenced in the case.

checklist.step: Contain the incident and preserve forensic evidence
actions: Isolate affected endpoints via CrowdStrike network containment and disable implicated accounts through the IAM platform.
Have the Incident Responder Digital Forensics Analyst capture memory and disk images before remediation alters evidence, hashing images into the case record.
Suspend implicated vendor data feeds pending the vendor's own containment attestations.
Log every containment action with actor and timestamp in the SOAR case.
checklist.done: containment actions and hashed forensic captures are logged before remediation proceeds.

checklist.step: Scope the data exposure to record and person level
actions: Query the affected systems to enumerate exactly which policyholders, SSNs/EINs, APH records or claim files were exposed, exporting the record-level list to the restricted case folder.
Distinguish accessed vs exfiltrated using DLP logs, netflow and access logs, and state the confidence level.
Deliver the scoped count and data classes to the Privacy Officer for notification analysis.
Update the case as scoping refines — each revision timestamped, none overwritten.
checklist.done: a record-level exposure list with data classes and exfiltration assessment sits in the restricted case folder.

checklist.step: Send the follow-up written report to FCIC as facts firm up
actions: Draft the supplemental written report covering scope, affected counts, root cause so far, containment and remediation plan, and have Legal Counsel clear it before transmission.
Send through the same RMA channel, referencing the original one-hour report, and file the copy with send date in the case.
Answer any RMA/FCIC follow-up questions within the timeframes RMA sets, tracking each ask in the case.
Correct earlier statements explicitly rather than silently — the record must show what was known when.
checklist.done: a cleared supplemental report is on file with FCIC and all RMA follow-ups are tracked to answer.

checklist.step: Run the state and individual notification analysis
actions: Map affected individuals to their states from the exposure list and determine each state's breach-notification trigger, threshold and deadline (commonly 30-60 days; some require AG notice above resident counts).
Decide harm-threshold positions where statutes allow, documenting the rationale per state.
Draft individual notification letters and any AG/regulator notices; the Privacy Officer approves content and the mailing schedule.
Record every jurisdiction's decision — notify or not, with cite — in the case.
checklist.done: every affected jurisdiction has a documented notify/no-notify decision with deadline and cite.

checklist.step: Execute individual notifications and remediation offers
actions: Mail approved notification letters within each state's deadline, using the document vendor under an executed FCIP data-sharing agreement.
Stand up the call-center script and FAQ with the Contact Center Ops Manager so agents answer policyholder questions consistently.
Arrange credit monitoring where offered and track enrollment codes issued.
File mailing certificates, the letter version and the mail date per individual into the case.
checklist.done: letters are mailed inside every state deadline with certificates filed and call-center support live.

checklist.step: Enforce the vendor flow-down clock on third-party incidents
actions: On any vendor notice, stamp the Company's discovery time as the moment the notice arrived — the one-hour FCIC clock runs from there, not from the vendor's internal discovery.
Demand the vendor's timeline and verify it met the immediate-notice flow-down in its agreement; a late vendor notice is a contract breach to log against the vendor record.
Obtain the vendor's forensic findings and containment attestations before restoring data feeds.
Feed vendor performance into the annual re-certification and, for material failures, the termination decision.
checklist.done: vendor incidents show a Company discovery stamp, a verified vendor timeline and a feed-restoration decision.

checklist.step: Close the incident with root cause and corrective actions
actions: Hold the post-incident review within 10 business days of containment: timeline, root cause, control failures and what would have shortened detection or reporting.
Raise corrective actions with owners and dates in the ticketing system, linked to the case.
Obtain the Privacy Officer's closure sign-off confirming FCIC, state and individual duties were all met.
Archive the complete case package to the compliance evidence repository under the reinsurance year.
checklist.done: a signed closure with root cause, corrective actions and an archived case package exists.

checklist.step: Drill the one-hour clock twice a year
actions: Run an unannounced tabletop injecting a suspected FCIP data exposure (e.g. adjuster laptop theft with unencrypted claim files) and measure wall-clock time from inject to simulated FCIC report.
Include an out-of-hours scenario annually so the paging chain is tested when primary contacts are asleep.
Score the drill against the 60-minute target and log misses as corrective actions.
Report drill results to the Chief Info Security Officer and file them with the runbook version tested.
checklist.done: two drills per year show measured time-to-report with corrective actions on any miss.

checklist.step: Reconcile incident tagging monthly so nothing escapes the FCIP queue
actions: Each month, sweep closed security tickets and DLP alerts for keywords and asset matches indicating crop policyholder data, comparing against cases that ran the FCIP playbook.
Investigate any incident on an FCIP-data asset that closed without the playbook and reclassify with a retrospective timeline.
Report reclassifications to the Privacy Officer immediately — a missed qualifying incident may still need late FCIC reporting with an explanation.
Track tagging-miss rate as a runbook KPI.
checklist.done: the monthly sweep is evidenced and any missed qualifying incident is reclassified and escalated.

checklist.step: Report incident-reporting posture to governance
actions: Report quarterly to the risk committee: qualifying incidents, time-to-report distribution against the 60-minute bar, drill results, vendor flow-down performance and open corrective actions.
Escalate any late or missed report with its root cause and the remediation state.
Minute the session and file the deck in the compliance evidence repository.
Feed systemic findings into the runbook's semi-annual refresh.
checklist.done: quarterly minutes show the time-to-report record and tracked corrective actions.

testing.step: Build the incident population from raw sources, not the FCIP queue
actions: Extract the period's security cases from the SIEM/SOAR, all 'lost device / data exposure' tickets from ServiceNow, DLP alerts, and vendor breach notices from the third-party register.
Filter to events touching FCIP-data-flagged assets or vendors, keeping events the SOC closed as non-incidents for re-screening.
Reconcile counts across sources and resolve gaps before sampling.
testing.done: a multi-source population including SOC-dismissed events is reconciled and documented.

testing.step: Re-screen dismissed events for missed qualifying incidents
actions: Independently re-read a random 25 dismissed events on FCIP-data assets and conclude whether each involved a loss or unauthorized disclosure, suspected or confirmed.
Treat any dismissed event that meets the Appendix III definition as a missed report — an automatic fail, not a judgement call.
Escalate live misses to the Privacy Officer the same day for late-reporting assessment.
testing.done: 25 dismissed events carry independent conclusions and any qualifying miss is escalated same-day.

testing.step: Sample reported incidents and reconstruct minute-level timelines
actions: Take 100% of incidents reported to FCIC in the period plus all vendor-notified events.
Rebuild each timeline from raw artifacts — alert timestamps, page acknowledgements, case notes, email send logs — not from the case summary.
Fix the true discovery moment (first human or system awareness) and compare against the stamped discovery time, noting any backdating.
testing.done: every reported incident has an independently reconstructed timeline anchored to raw artifacts.

testing.step: Recompute the one-hour clock on every sampled incident
actions: Compute minutes from true discovery to the FCIC report send time evidenced in the case.
Score each incident pass/fail against 60 minutes; a report awaiting 'confirmation' before sending fails the no-distinction rule regardless of final timing.
For vendor events, compute from the vendor notice arrival time and separately assess the vendor's own flow-down timeliness.
Tabulate the time-to-report distribution for the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled incident shows a computed time-to-report and a pass/fail against 60 minutes.

testing.step: Verify report content and channel against the runbook
actions: Read each FCIC report copy and confirm it named the AIP, discovery time, incident nature, data classes and containment state, and went through the RMA-designated channel on the contact card.
Confirm the supplemental written report followed and was cleared by Legal Counsel before sending.
Flag reports sent to stale contacts or informal channels as exceptions.
testing.done: sampled reports show complete content, cleared follow-ups and the correct channel.

testing.step: Trace state and individual notifications to statutory deadlines
actions: For each incident with individual exposure, re-derive the state deadline set from the affected-resident mapping and compare mailing certificates against each deadline.
Verify AG/regulator notices went where resident counts triggered them, with copies on file.
Check no-notify decisions carry Privacy Counsel rationale and cites.
Any missed statutory deadline is a reportable exception with the day count overrun stated.
testing.done: all notifications trace to on-time mailing certificates or exceptions state the overrun.

testing.step: Verify forensic evidence and exposure scoping integrity
actions: Confirm forensic images exist with matching hashes for sampled incidents and that scoping queries and record-level lists are preserved in the restricted folder.
Cross-check the affected count reported to FCIC in the supplemental report against the final scoped list, noting unexplained variances.
Verify containment timestamps precede remediation actions in the case log.
testing.done: forensics, scoping and reported counts reconcile for every sampled incident.

testing.step: Observe and score the unannounced drill
actions: Attend the period's unannounced tabletop as observer and independently time inject-to-simulated-report.
Verify the paging chain fired as designed and the on-call responders, not just leadership, executed the runbook.
Compare the observed time against the 60-minute target and against the SOC's own scoring for consistency.
testing.done: the drill is independently timed and scored with any variance from SOC scoring explained.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception: late report, missed qualifying incident, notification overrun or drill failure, each with its minute/day quantification.
Assign root cause (tagging miss, paging failure, confirmation-first behavior, vendor delay) and an accountable owner with a date.
For unreported qualifying incidents, confirm the late-report decision with Legal Counsel and the Privacy Officer is documented.
Carry open exceptions into the next semi-annual test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception is quantified, owned, dated and carries a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — against the zero-tolerance one-hour threshold, citing the time-to-report distribution and drill result.
Have the independent reviewer, segregated from the SOC reporting line, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Chief Info Security Officer, Privacy Officer and risk committee, and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and the time-to-report record is filed and reported.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual with continuous new-hire intake; test runs annually after cycle close plus a mid-year spot check on new-hire 30-day compliance

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Learning & Development and the Privacy Office

Regulator response path.value: The Compliance Manager fields RMA training inquiries; the Privacy Officer supplies curriculum and completion evidence and Legal Counsel clears responses

checklist.step: Derive the training population from access, not job titles
actions: Pull the active-worker roster (employees and contingent workers) from the HRIS with job code, department and manager.
Join the IAM entitlement extract of users provisioned to FCIP-data-flagged systems supplied by the Access Management Analyst.
Add vendor loss adjusters from the rosters filed with vendor agreements, coordinating with the Vendor Manager.
Deliver the deduplicated population file to Learning & Development with a dated snapshot label.
checklist.done: a dated, access-derived population file covering employees, contractors and vendor adjusters exists.

checklist.step: Refresh the curriculum against the current SRA and Manual 14
actions: Map each module to its source: Appendix III data classes and handling rules, the one-hour incident-reporting duty and who to call, the FCIP-only data-use restriction, secure transmission rules for the weekly transaction-cutoff data submissions, and clean-desk/paper-file handling for field adjusters.
Update scenarios with the prior year's real incident patterns supplied by the Privacy Officer (anonymized).
Write a 10-question mastery quiz with an 80% pass bar and question-bank rotation.
Route the refreshed content to the Privacy Officer and Compliance Manager for documented approval before publication.
checklist.done: the curriculum carries a source-mapping table and dated approvals for the current reinsurance year.

checklist.step: Build role-specific tracks for high-exposure audiences
actions: Configure tracks in Cornerstone: base privacy module for all; an adjuster supplement covering field handling of claim files, photographs and producer conversations per LASH; a data-team supplement on Appendix III extract handling and the weekly cutoff pipeline.
Set audience rules so track assignment follows the population file's role flags automatically.
Pilot each track with five users per audience and fix comprehension failures before launch.
Version-stamp published tracks with the curriculum approval reference.
checklist.done: role tracks are configured, piloted and version-stamped in the LMS.

checklist.step: Launch the annual assignment with a hard completion window
actions: Load the population file and mass-assign the correct track with a due date 30 days out, timed so the cycle closes before the reinsurance-year contract change date.
Verify assignment counts equal the population file line count and investigate any shortfall same-day.
Announce the cycle through the Communications Specialist with the Privacy Officer as sender for weight.
Snapshot the opening assignment list into the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: assignments equal the population count and the opening snapshot is filed.

checklist.step: Auto-assign training on new hire or new FCIP access
actions: Configure the HRIS-to-LMS feed to assign the track on hire events into flagged job codes, due 30 days from start date.
Configure the IAM provisioning workflow to fire an LMS assignment whenever a user gains access to an FCIP-data system mid-year.
Test both triggers monthly with a synthetic hire and a synthetic entitlement grant, filing the test evidence.
Reconcile weekly: new FCIP-data entitlements against new assignments, chasing gaps immediately.
checklist.done: both auto-assignment triggers pass monthly tests and the weekly reconciliation shows no unassigned new access.

checklist.step: Chase completion and escalate past-due users
actions: Let Cornerstone send reminders at 15 and 30 days; at 45 days past due, export the delinquent list with managers and send the escalation pack to each manager and the Privacy Officer.
Flag delinquent users holding Protected Information access to the Access Management Analyst for the suspend/retain decision.
Record each retention decision and its mitigation in the exception log.
Track completion rate weekly to the Privacy Officer until the cycle closes.
checklist.done: past-45-day users have a recorded access decision and the weekly rate reaches the cycle target.

checklist.step: Verify quiz mastery and remediate failures
actions: Run the quiz-results report; completion without an 80% pass is not completion.
Allow two retakes with rotated questions; route third failures to live remediation with the Trainer and the user's manager.
Record remediation outcomes so no user shows complete without a passing score.
Summarize commonly missed questions to the Instructional Designer for next-cycle content fixes.
checklist.done: every completion carries a passing score or a documented live remediation.

checklist.step: Run pre-season proficiency training for loss adjusters
actions: Schedule the adjuster privacy-and-handling sessions ahead of the crop-year sales closing dates so field staff are trained before season workload peaks.
Cover LASH-aligned handling: claim-file custody, photo and geospatial data care, producer/policyholder conversations and the lost-file reporting drill into the one-hour clock.
Collect signed attendance and store certificates in the LMS against each adjuster, including vendor adjusters via their firm coordinators.
Report adjuster completion separately to the Claims Director / Manager and the Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: adjuster sessions complete pre-season with certificates filed for staff and vendor adjusters.

checklist.step: Cover vendor personnel through the flow-down
actions: Collect each data-access vendor's annual attestation that its FCIP-assigned personnel completed equivalent privacy training, as required by the agreement's training clause.
Spot-check two named vendor staff per major vendor by requesting their certificates.
Log non-attesting vendors as exceptions to the Compliance Manager with the access decision.
File attestations with the vendor contract records.
checklist.done: every data-access vendor holds a current attestation with spot-check evidence filed.

checklist.step: Close the annual cycle with a completion attestation
actions: Reconcile final completions against the access-derived population and compute the closing rate.
Review the exception log — every incomplete user must show an access decision, not a blank.
Sign the annual completion attestation stating rate, exceptions and decisions, and file it with the closing snapshot in the compliance evidence repository.
Report the close to the Chief HR Officer and Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: a signed attestation with the closing rate and dispositioned exceptions is filed.

checklist.step: Keep training evidence retrievable for RMA review
actions: File curriculum versions, source mappings, approvals, opening/closing snapshots and the attestation under the reinsurance year with the 3-year retention label.
Index per-person certificates so any named individual's record retrieves within 2 business days.
Test retrieval annually with three random names, filing the test note.
Confirm vendor attestations cross-reference from the vendor contract records.
checklist.done: the evidence set is labeled, indexed and passes the named-person retrieval test.

checklist.step: Handle mid-year SRA or Appendix III changes with delta training
actions: Monitor RMA bulletins and the SRA reissue for handling-rule changes; assess training impact within 45 days of publication.
Commission a short delta module for material changes rather than waiting for the next annual cycle.
Assign the delta to the affected audience with a 30-day window and track it like the annual cycle.
Record the change-to-training decision trail even when the decision is no delta needed.
checklist.done: every RMA change shows a dated impact decision and, where material, a completed delta assignment.

checklist.step: Monitor training effectiveness against incident data
actions: Quarterly, compare privacy incident and DLP-alert patterns from the SOC against training content coverage.
Flag recurring human-error patterns (misdirected email, unencrypted extracts) to the Instructional Designer for targeted content.
Track whether repeat offenders completed training and escalate pattern cases to their managers with the Employee Relations Manager.
File the quarterly effectiveness note with the training records.
checklist.done: quarterly effectiveness notes exist and drive documented content or conduct actions.

checklist.step: Enforce completion at access recertification
actions: Include current-cycle training completion as a certification attribute in the quarterly FCIP-data access reviews in the IAM platform.
Route incomplete users to their certifying manager with the options: complete within 15 days or lose the entitlement.
Execute removals for users still incomplete at the review close and record them.
Report removals to the Privacy Officer for the exception log.
checklist.done: quarterly access reviews show training status checked and removals executed for non-completion.

checklist.step: Log and remediate training exceptions
actions: Raise a tracker issue for systemic failures: feed breaks that missed assignments, audiences omitted from the population, or vendor attestation refusals.
Assign root cause and an owner with a remediation date; the Privacy Officer signs closure.
Carry systemic exceptions into the annual verification test as mandatory retest areas.
Summarize the exception picture in the annual attestation.
checklist.done: systemic exceptions are tracked, owned, signed off and fed to the annual test.

testing.step: Independently rebuild the population from IAM and HRIS
actions: Extract all users holding entitlements to FCIP-data-flagged systems at any point in the reinsurance year from IAM history.
Join HRIS records for employment dates and add vendor adjuster rosters from contract files.
Compare the rebuilt population to the file Learning & Development used; unexplained differences are findings before any sampling.
testing.done: an independently rebuilt population exists and differences from the operational file are explained or logged.

testing.step: Reconcile completions to the rebuilt population
actions: Match every rebuilt-population member to an LMS completion with a passing quiz score in the cycle.
Compute the true completion rate against the 98% threshold using the rebuilt denominator, not the LMS assignment count.
List every Protected-Information-access user incomplete beyond 45 days as an individual exception.
testing.done: a true completion rate is computed on the independent denominator with individual exceptions listed.

testing.step: Sample and trace individual completion evidence
actions: Draw 25 users (seeded, reproducible): 10 adjusters, 5 data-team users, 5 new hires, 5 contractors/vendor staff.
Trace each to certificate, completion timestamp, quiz score and the curriculum version taken.
For new hires, recompute days from start date (or access-grant date) to completion against the 30-day rule.
testing.done: all 25 traces show valid certificates, passing scores and 30-day maths for new hires.

testing.step: Verify curriculum content against the SRA sources
actions: Take the delivered curriculum version and independently verify the source mapping: Appendix III handling rules, the one-hour reporting duty with correct contacts, FCIP-only use, and cutoff-data transmission rules all present and current.
Check the version delivered matches the version the Privacy Officer approved.
Flag stale content — e.g. superseded RMA contacts or prior-year SRA cites — as findings.
testing.done: the delivered curriculum verifiably maps to current SRA/Manual 14 content and matches its approval.

testing.step: Test the auto-assignment triggers with real events
actions: Select 10 real mid-year FCIP-access grants from IAM history and confirm each generated an LMS assignment within the feed SLA.
Select 10 real hires into flagged job codes and confirm the same.
Any grant or hire without a timely assignment is an exception, and the weekly reconciliation that should have caught it is a second finding.
testing.done: 20 real trigger events trace to timely assignments or exceptions plus reconciliation findings are logged.

testing.step: Verify past-due escalation and access decisions actually happened
actions: For every user who crossed 45 days past due in the cycle, pull the escalation pack, the manager response and the recorded suspend/retain decision.
Trace suspended users to actual entitlement removal in IAM logs with dates.
A retained user with no documented mitigation is an exception against the procedure.
testing.done: every past-45-day case shows an escalation, a decision and, where suspended, an executed removal.

testing.step: Verify adjuster pre-season sessions and vendor attestations
actions: Check adjuster session dates fell before the relevant sales closing dates and trace 5 staff plus 5 vendor adjusters to certificates.
Verify each major data-access vendor's annual training attestation is on file with its spot-check evidence.
Cross-check two vendor adjusters who worked claims in the period against the certificates their firm attested to.
testing.done: pre-season timing holds, sampled certificates exist and vendor attestations withstand the cross-check.

testing.step: Verify the access-recertification enforcement loop
actions: Open the quarterly FCIP-data access reviews and confirm training status appeared as a certification attribute.
Trace users flagged incomplete at review to either completion within 15 days or entitlement removal.
Flag reviews where certifiers approved incomplete users without the documented options being exercised.
testing.done: access reviews demonstrably enforced the training condition or exceptions are logged.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with the person or process affected, the defect and the exposure window.
Assign root cause (population miss, feed break, escalation not executed, stale content) and an accountable owner with a date.
Require the Privacy Officer's sign-off on each closure.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception is owned, dated, signed off at closure and committed to retest.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the true completion rate against 98% and the individual-exception count, and state the conclusion: effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective.
Have the independent reviewer — outside Learning & Development and the Privacy Office — sign the workpaper.
Report to the Privacy Officer, Chief HR Officer and Head of Compliance, and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with the true rate, exceptions and a stated conclusion is filed.
