checklist.step: Run the close calendar and lock the crop ledger on schedule
actions: Publish the quarter's close calendar in BlackLine working back from the blank's filing deadline (March 1 annual; May 15 / August 15 / November 15 quarterlies), assigning each task an owner and due date.
Lock the SAP S/4HANA crop-company ledger at the calendar cut and control late entries through documented top-side adjustments only.
Track task completion daily in the close dashboard and escalate slippage over 1 day to the Chief Financial Officer.
Archive the completed calendar as close evidence.
checklist.done: the ledger locks on the calendar date and every close task shows an owner and completion timestamp.

checklist.step: Account for FCIC ceded and retained business by fund designation
actions: Post crop premium and loss entries split by the SRA fund designations (Assigned Risk Fund and Commercial Funds) and by retained vs FCIC-ceded share, using the designation data from the policy admin extract.
Reconcile booked ceded premium and loss balances to the RMA settlement/escrow activity for the period, itemizing timing differences.
Apply SSAP 78 treatment for the federal crop program and document any permitted-practice positions with the domiciliary state.
Post the underwriting-gain/loss sharing accrual per the SRA formula and retain the calculation workpaper.
checklist.done: fund-designated balances reconcile to RMA settlement activity with SSAP 78 workpapers on file.

checklist.step: Reconcile company data to RMA weekly submissions before close
actions: Pull the cumulative premium and loss data accepted by RMA through the weekly transaction cutoffs for the period from the data-submission team.
Reconcile to the general ledger crop balances, investigating differences over the materiality threshold with the Data Quality Analyst.
Correct rejected or pending transactions with the processing team no later than the next weekly transaction cutoff.
File the reconciliation with sign-off in BlackLine.
checklist.done: GL crop balances reconcile to RMA-accepted data with differences dispositioned and the sign-off filed.

checklist.step: Prepare the statement blanks in the statutory software
actions: Load the locked trial balance into the statutory reporting software and map to the annual/quarterly P&C blank lines for the statement year.
Complete the crop-relevant pages: Underwriting & Investment Exhibit, state page premium allocations, Schedule F for FCIC and private cessions, and Schedule P crop lines.
Run the software's cross-check edits and clear every failed edit with a documented explanation, not an override.
Route the draft blank to the Controller for page-by-page review sign-off.
checklist.done: the draft blank passes cross-checks with cleared edits and carries the Controller's review sign-off.

checklist.step: Tie out every blank page to workpapers
actions: Prepare a tie-out binder linking each material blank line to its source workpaper, reconciliation or subledger extract.
Agree Schedule F ceded balances to the reinsurance administration system and treaty statements.
Agree Schedule P development to the Reserving Actuary's triangles and the actuarial opinion data.
Have a second accountant initial each tie-out independently.
checklist.done: a dual-initialed tie-out binder covers every material line with source references.

checklist.step: Inventory and document every private reinsurance arrangement
actions: List from the treaty repository every private (non-FCIC) reinsurance arrangement touching eligible crop insurance contracts in force during the year — stop-loss, quota share and any affiliate arrangements.
Record per arrangement: reinsurer, terms, effective dates, and whether collateral or licensure supports credit under the NAIC Credit for Reinsurance Model Law.
Flag new or amended arrangements since the last FCIC disclosure for the disclosure letter.
Deliver the inventory to the Reinsurance Manager for completeness confirmation.
checklist.done: a confirmed inventory of private crop reinsurance arrangements with credit-eligibility notes exists.

checklist.step: Verify each private arrangement meets NAIC credit-for-reinsurance standards
actions: For each arrangement, verify the reinsurer is licensed, accredited, certified or reciprocal in the domiciliary state, or that qualifying collateral (trust, letter of credit, funds withheld) is in place per the NAIC Credit for Reinsurance Model Law.
Check the arrangement's accounting follows the NAIC Accounting Practices and Procedures Manual, including risk-transfer analysis under SSAP 62R.
Document the conclusion per arrangement and route failures to the Head of Reinsurance for restructuring before year-end.
File the credit analysis with the treaty record.
checklist.done: every arrangement carries a documented credit-standard conclusion and failures have a restructuring path.

checklist.step: Send the written private reinsurance disclosure to FCIC
actions: Draft the disclosure letter to FCIC describing each private reinsurance arrangement on eligible crop contracts — parties, structure, limits, effective dates — as SRA Section II(b)(11) requires.
Attach the credit-standard conclusions and have the Chief Financial Officer approve the letter.
Transmit to RMA with the Plan of Operations package by April 1, or immediately on entering a new arrangement mid-year, and retain proof of transmission.
Log RMA's acknowledgement and any follow-up requests, answering within 45 days of the FCIC ask.
checklist.done: a CFO-approved disclosure covering every in-force arrangement is transmitted with proof and logged responses.

checklist.step: Obtain the actuarial opinion and management certifications
actions: Issue the Statement of Actuarial Opinion on crop reserves consistent with the Schedule P data, delivering the opinion and summary by the annual-statement date.
Reconcile opinion data exhibits to the filed blank and resolve differences before signing.
Provide the Actuarial Opinion Summary to the domiciliary state by its due date (typically March 15).
File the opinion, summary and reliance letters in the financial reporting repository.
checklist.done: the signed opinion reconciles to the blank and the summary is delivered on time.

checklist.step: Execute the jurat and file with NAIC and the domiciliary state
actions: Obtain officer signatures and notarization on the jurat page per the blank instructions.

Submit the electronic filing to the NAIC by March 1 (annual) or the quarterly dates through the statutory software's NAIC submission function, and file hard copies where the domiciliary state still requires them.
Capture the NAIC submission confirmation and store it with the filed statement.
Confirm the filing passed NAIC validations; fix and resubmit any rejection within 3 business days.
checklist.done: the executed statement is filed on time with the NAIC confirmation captured and validations passed.

checklist.step: Prepare the FCIC financial exhibit package for the Plan of Operations
actions: Compile the financial exhibits RMA requires with the annual Plan of Operations: latest filed statutory statements, surplus and RBC evidence of financial capacity, projected crop writings by state and fund, and the maximum reinsurable premium computation.
Tie every exhibit figure to the filed blank or the board-approved plan, noting sources on each page.
Deliver the package to the Regulatory Affairs Manager for the April 1 submission to RMA.
File the transmitted package and RMA's acceptance in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the exhibit package ties to filed statements and is with RMA by April 1 with acceptance filed.

checklist.step: Answer regulator and RMA financial queries on the record
actions: Log every NAIC analyst, state or RMA financial query in the close-issue log with its due date — RMA requests carry the 45-day response target.
Prepare responses tied to filed figures, with the Controller reviewing before release.
Track amended-filing decisions: material errors trigger an amended statement with the domiciliary state and NAIC, filed with an explanatory letter.
Close each query with the response copy filed alongside the statement.
checklist.done: every query shows a logged due date, a reviewed response and filed correspondence.

checklist.step: Maintain the crop data submission linkage file for exam readiness
actions: Maintain a standing crosswalk from filed statement lines to RMA-accepted cumulative data, updated each quarter after the reconciliation closes.
Note explained differences (timing, fund designation, escrow cutoff) with amounts so an examiner can follow the bridge without the preparer.
Store the crosswalk with the statement package in the financial reporting repository.
Refresh the crosswalk within 45 days of any RMA data correction that changes prior-period figures.
checklist.done: a current statement-to-RMA-data crosswalk with explained differences accompanies each filed statement.

checklist.step: Update procedures for blanks and SRA changes each year
actions: Review the NAIC blanks adoptions for the coming statement year and the new SRA/amendments each July, listing impacts on crop pages and disclosures.
Update the close procedure, tie-out templates and statutory software mappings before the first affected quarter.
Brief the close team on changes at the pre-close meeting with documented attendance.
Version the procedure and file the change log.
checklist.done: the procedure and mappings reflect current blanks and SRA text before the first affected close.

checklist.step: Log and remediate filing exceptions
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any late filing, failed validation resubmission, undisclosed arrangement or material tie-out break, quantifying the miss.
Assign root cause (close slippage, mapping error, treaty inventory gap) and an owner with a date.
Obtain CFO sign-off on closure and on any amended filing.
Carry exceptions into the annual verification test as mandatory retest rows.
checklist.done: every exception is quantified, owned, CFO-signed at closure and committed to retest.

testing.step: Build the filing and arrangement population
actions: List the statement year's required filings — annual blank, three quarterlies, actuarial opinion and summary, and the FCIC April 1 exhibit package — from the blanks instructions and SRA, not from the close calendar.
Extract every private reinsurance arrangement on crop business in force during the year from the treaty repository and ceded-accounting records.
Reconcile the arrangement list to reinsurance expense in the GL so unbooked or unlisted treaties surface.
testing.done: an independent population of required filings and in-force private arrangements is documented.

testing.step: Verify every filing met its deadline
actions: Pull the NAIC submission confirmations and compare each timestamp to March 1 / May 15 / August 15 / November 15.
Verify the FCIC exhibit package transmittal proof against April 1.
Check rejected validations were resubmitted within 3 business days by tracing the resubmission timestamps.
testing.done: every filing shows a confirmation timestamp on or before its deadline or a quantified exception.

testing.step: Re-perform the blank-to-workpaper tie-out on sampled lines
actions: Select 15 material lines across the Underwriting & Investment Exhibit, state page, Schedule F and Schedule P (seeded, reproducible).
Independently agree each filed figure to the source workpaper, subledger or reconciliation without using the preparer's binder as the starting point.
Log any difference above the clearly-trivial threshold with its amount.
testing.done: 15 sampled lines independently tie to source or differences are quantified.

testing.step: Reconcile filed crop figures to RMA-accepted data
actions: Re-run the statement-to-RMA-data bridge for the annual statement using the cumulative accepted-data extract as of the final weekly transaction cutoff of the year.
Verify each bridging difference is one of the documented types (timing, fund designation, escrow cutoff) with support.
An unexplained difference above materiality is an exception against the reconciliation control.
testing.done: the bridge re-performs with all differences explained or exceptions quantified.

testing.step: Trace every private arrangement to a written FCIC disclosure
actions: Match each in-force arrangement from the independent population to a line in a transmitted FCIC disclosure letter.
Check mid-year arrangements were disclosed at inception, not held for the next April 1 package, by comparing treaty effective dates to letter dates.
An undisclosed in-force arrangement is an automatic fail escalated to the CFO the same day.
testing.done: every arrangement traces to a timely written disclosure or the fail is escalated same-day.

testing.step: Re-perform the credit-for-reinsurance conclusions on a sample
actions: For 5 sampled arrangements, independently verify reinsurer status (licensed/accredited/certified/reciprocal) against the domiciliary state's company search and collateral documents.
Re-read the SSAP 62R risk-transfer memo and confirm the conclusion is supported, not asserted.
Compare Schedule F presentation to the verified status, flagging misclassified credit.
testing.done: sampled arrangements show independently verified credit status consistent with Schedule F.

testing.step: Verify the actuarial opinion linkage
actions: Agree the opinion's Exhibit A/B data to the filed Schedule P crop lines.
Confirm the opinion and Actuarial Opinion Summary delivery dates met their deadlines.
Check reliance and data-quality caveats were disclosed to the Controller and considered in the close-issue log.
testing.done: opinion data agrees to the blank and deadlines and caveats are evidenced.

testing.step: Verify the FCIC exhibit package ties to filed statements
actions: Agree surplus, RBC and premium-capacity figures in the April 1 package to the filed annual statement and RBC filing.
Recompute the maximum reinsurable premium calculation from its stated inputs.
Verify RMA's acceptance correspondence is on file and any RMA follow-ups were answered within 45 days.
testing.done: the exhibit package recomputes and ties to filed statements with RMA acceptance evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with the filing or arrangement affected, the defect and the quantified miss.
Assign root cause (calendar slippage, mapping error, inventory gap, disclosure lag) and an accountable owner with a date.
Confirm amended-filing decisions for material errors are documented with the domiciliary state.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception is quantified, owned, dated and committed to retest.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — against the on-time-filing and full-disclosure thresholds.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared or approved none of the tested items, sign the workpaper.
Report to the CFO and Audit Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the CFO and Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Build the annual filing calendar from source checklists
actions: Each January, rebuild the calendar from the NAIC Annual Statement Instructions filing schedule and every licensed state's current-year filing checklist downloaded from the state site — never roll forward last year's dates unverified.
Add crop-specific entries: the RMA Plan of Operations due April 1, state premium tax returns on crop premium, and any state crop-assessment filings.
Enter each filing in the tracker with jurisdiction, form, due date, owner, submission channel (NAIC portal, state portal, paper) and fee.
Have the Regulatory Reporting Manager approve the completed calendar and lock it.
checklist.done: an approved, locked calendar built from current-year checklists covers NAIC, states and RMA entries.

checklist.step: Verify state applicability for every licensed state with crop premium
actions: Pull the licensed-state list and prior-year state page premium by state from the filed annual statement.
For each state with crop premium, read its checklist for supplemental filings (state-specific interrogatories, premium tax, fraud assessments) and confirm each is on the calendar.
For zero-premium licensed states, record whether the state still requires a statement filing or accepts the NAIC filing.
Document the applicability conclusion per state with the checklist citation.
checklist.done: every licensed state has a documented applicability conclusion with citations, reflected on the calendar.

checklist.step: Assign owners and stage internal due dates ahead of each deadline
actions: Assign a preparer and a reviewer per filing, with the internal completion date at least 5 business days before the regulatory deadline.
Sequence dependencies: the annual blank must be filed before state copies, RBC and most supplements can go.
Configure tracker alerts at T-30/T-15/T-5 and the T-5 escalation to the Controller.
Brief owners at the January calendar kickoff with documented attendance.
checklist.done: every filing shows a preparer, reviewer, staged internal date and armed alerts.

checklist.step: Submit NAIC electronic filings and capture confirmations
actions: Submit the annual statement by March 1 and quarterlies by May 15 / August 15 / November 15 through the statutory software's NAIC submission function.
Run pre-submission validations and clear failures before transmitting; never transmit with overridden errors.
Save the NAIC submission confirmation PDF to the filing evidence log the same day.
Monitor the NAIC status for acceptance and cure any rejection within 3 business days, logging the resubmission confirmation.
checklist.done: each NAIC filing shows a same-day confirmation and any rejection cured inside 3 business days.

checklist.step: File state statement copies and supplemental filings per checklist
actions: For states requiring direct filings, submit via the state portal or paper per the checklist, enclosing signed jurats, checklists and fees as specified.
Pay filing fees through the approved payment method and staple the payment evidence to the filing record.
Capture the portal receipt or certified-mail evidence for every state filing in the evidence log.
Mark each tracker entry complete only when the filed copy and receipt are both attached.
checklist.done: every state filing shows a filed copy plus receipt and its tracker entry closed on evidence.

checklist.step: File the RBC report and audited financials on their own clocks
actions: File the RBC report with the NAIC and domiciliary state by March 1, tying the inputs to the filed annual statement.
File the audited statutory financial statements by June 1 to the domiciliary state and states requiring copies, coordinating delivery with the Controller.
Capture confirmations for both into the evidence log.
Track the accountant's awareness letter and any required communication of material weaknesses to the state.
checklist.done: RBC and audited financials are filed by March 1 and June 1 with confirmations logged.

checklist.step: Submit the Plan of Operations to RMA by April 1
actions: Assemble the Plan of Operations for the coming reinsurance year — financial exhibits from the Financial Analyst, state/fund writing projections, subcontractor exhibit from the Compliance Manager — per the current SRA and RMA instructions.
Obtain CFO approval of the complete package.
Submit to RMA through the designated channel by April 1 and retain proof of transmission.
Track RMA's review questions and respond within 45 days of each FCIC request, logging correspondence.
checklist.done: the approved Plan of Operations is with RMA by April 1 with transmission proof and tracked responses.

checklist.step: Coordinate crop premium tax and assessment filings
actions: Prepare state premium tax returns reflecting crop premium by state from the state pages, applying each state's treatment of federally reinsured crop premium where exemptions exist.
Document the taxability position per state with citation; where crop premium is exempt, retain the exemption support.
File returns and payments by each state's due date via its tax portal and log the receipts.
Reconcile total taxed premium across returns to the annual statement state page totals.
checklist.done: premium tax filings reconcile to state pages with per-state positions documented and receipts logged.

checklist.step: Run the weekly evidence sweep during filing season
actions: Each Friday from February through June, sweep the tracker for filings marked complete without both the filed copy and confirmation attached.
Chase missing evidence with the filing owner the same day and reopen entries lacking it.
Report the sweep result (entries checked, evidence gaps) to the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
File the weekly sweep notes as calendar-control evidence.
checklist.done: weekly sweeps are evidenced and no closed entry lacks its filed copy and confirmation.

checklist.step: Handle regulator rejections and correction requests
actions: Log every rejection or correction request the day it arrives with its cure deadline; the internal standard is resubmission within 3 business days.
Route the correction to the original preparer with reviewer re-check before resubmission.
Where a correction changes a filed figure materially, trigger the amended-filing assessment with the Controller.
Record the resubmission confirmation and the regulator's acceptance.
checklist.done: every rejection shows a same-day log entry, a resubmission within 3 business days and an acceptance record.

checklist.step: Monitor checklist and deadline changes mid-year
actions: Subscribe to NAIC blanks updates and state bulletin feeds; check monthly for filing-requirement changes affecting the calendar.
Update the locked calendar through a change-control entry approved by the Regulatory Reporting Manager, never by silent edit.
Notify affected filing owners of date or content changes immediately.
Keep the change log with the calendar as evidence the calendar stayed current.
checklist.done: calendar changes flow through approved change-control entries with owners notified.

checklist.step: Maintain the consolidated evidence log for exam production
actions: File each filing's package — filed copy, confirmation, acknowledgement, fee evidence — in the financial reporting repository indexed by year, jurisdiction and form.
Apply the 3-year retention label (or the longer state-specific period where required).
Test retrieval quarterly with two random filings against a 2-business-day standard.
Fix indexing gaps found by the test and note the fix.
checklist.done: the indexed evidence log passes quarterly retrieval tests with retention labels applied.

checklist.step: Escalate at-risk filings before the deadline, not after
actions: At every T-5 alert where the filing is not in review, escalate to the Controller with the blocker named.
Where a miss is unavoidable, contact the regulator before the deadline to request an extension or advise the delay, with the Controller approving the communication.
Document the regulator's response and the revised date on the tracker entry.
Treat every near-miss as a lesson: record the blocker in the calendar retrospective.
checklist.done: at-risk filings show pre-deadline escalation and, where late, pre-deadline regulator contact.

checklist.step: Run the post-season calendar retrospective
actions: After June 1, review the season: on-time rate, near-misses, rejections, evidence-sweep findings and regulator feedback.
Agree calendar-build and staffing changes for next year with the Controller.
Document the retrospective and its actions with owners.
File the retrospective with the calendar records.
checklist.done: a documented retrospective with owned actions closes the filing season.

checklist.step: Log and remediate filing exceptions
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every late, omitted or rejected-uncured filing with the day count and penalty exposure.
Assign root cause (dependency slip, checklist miss, portal failure) and an owner with a date.
Obtain Controller sign-off on closure and on any penalty payment or regulator commitment.
Carry exceptions into the annual verification test as mandatory retest rows.
checklist.done: every filing exception is quantified, owned, Controller-signed and committed to retest.

testing.step: Rebuild the due-filing population independently
actions: Rebuild the statement year's required filings from the NAIC instructions and each licensed state's own checklist pulled fresh from state sites — without reference to the Company's calendar.
Add the RMA Plan of Operations (April 1), RBC (March 1), audited financials (June 1) and premium tax returns for states with crop premium.
Compare the rebuilt list to the Company calendar; any due filing absent from the calendar is a calendar-control fail regardless of whether it was filed.
testing.done: an independently rebuilt filing list exists and calendar omissions are logged as control fails.

testing.step: Sample-verify state supplemental filings in depth

testing.step: Verify NAIC validation and rejection handling

testing.step: Verify the April 1 RMA submission and follow-ups

Confirm the package version transmitted matches the approved version.

testing.step: Recompute premium tax reconciliation on a sample

Trace payment receipts against each state's due date.
testing.done: sampled returns reconcile to state pages with supported positions and timely payments.

testing.step: Test the weekly evidence sweep and T-5 escalation controls
actions: Pull the Friday sweep notes for February–June and verify the sweeps ran and reopened entries lacking evidence.
Pull tracker alert history for 5 filings and confirm the T-5 escalation fired where the filing was not in review.
Check near-miss filings show pre-deadline regulator contact where a miss occurred.

testing.step: Test evidence retrieval speed
actions: Request three named filings' full packages from the Records Manager and time retrieval against the 2-business-day standard.
Check retention labels on the retrieved packages match the required period.
Verify the quarterly retrieval self-tests were performed and documented.
testing.done: packages retrieve on time with correct labels and self-tests evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date

Assign root cause (calendar omission, dependency slip, evidence gap) and an accountable owner with a date.
Verify prior-year exceptions were retested and closed before accepting new closures.
Carry open items into next year's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception is quantified, owned, dated and prior-year retests are verified.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report

checklist.step: Confirm the year's supplemental inventory from the instructions
actions: Each January, list every schedule, exhibit and interrogatory the current NAIC instructions require for a P&C company with crop business, noting new or changed items for the statement year.
Add state-required supplements from the filing checklists and the RMA exhibit set due April 1.
Assign each item a preparer, reviewer and close-calendar date feeding the March 1 and April 1 deadlines.
Have the Controller approve the inventory as the season's scope.
checklist.done: an approved inventory covers every required schedule, supplement and exhibit with owners and dates.

checklist.step: Stage source extracts with documented lineage
actions: Pull the locked trial balance, the ceded balances from the reinsurance administration system, the loss triangles from the Reserving Analyst, and the state premium allocation from the policy admin extract.
Stamp each extract with run date, source system, query reference and record count on the lineage sheet.
Store extracts read-only in the schedule workpaper folder so preparers work from identical data.
Refresh and re-stamp any extract rerun after adjustments — never overwrite the original.
checklist.done: all source extracts are staged read-only with lineage stamps and no schedule is built on unstamped data.

checklist.step: Prepare Schedule F for FCIC and private cessions
actions: Report the FCIC cession on its own Schedule F line with the federal reinsurer identification per the instructions, and each private reinsurer with its NAIC company code, domicile and status classification.
Populate ceded premium, recoverables on paid and unpaid losses and provision for reinsurance from the staged ceded extract.
Compute the provision for reinsurance per the Schedule F penalty methodology for any unsecured or overdue balances, retaining the calculation.
Agree Schedule F totals to the ledger ceded balances and to the treaty statements from the Ceded Reinsurance Analyst.
checklist.done: Schedule F presents FCIC and private cessions correctly with the provision computed and totals agreed.

checklist.step: Prepare Schedule P crop lines from reserving data
actions: Populate the Schedule P parts for the crop line from the staged triangles: premiums earned, losses and expenses paid and incurred by accident year, net of the FCIC cession.
Reconcile the current diagonal to the ledger loss balances and the prior-year statement's Schedule P for one-year and two-year development consistency.
Have the Reserving Actuary review the completed parts against the data supporting the actuarial opinion.
Document any restatement or reallocation with the reason and amount.
checklist.done: Schedule P crop lines reconcile to the ledger, prior statement and opinion data with actuary review recorded.

checklist.step: Prepare Schedule T and the state pages
actions: Allocate crop direct premium, losses and dividends by state from the policy admin extract, using risk location per the instructions.
Complete Schedule T licensing status per state against the licensed-state list from the Regulatory Reporting Analyst.
Cross-check state page totals to the Underwriting & Investment Exhibit and Schedule T to the state pages.
Investigate any state showing premium without a license and escalate to the Compliance Manager immediately.
checklist.done: state pages and Schedule T cross-foot to the exhibit with licensing consistency verified.

checklist.step: Answer the general and supplemental interrogatories
actions: Draft interrogatory answers with input owners named per question — reinsurance questions to the Reinsurance Manager, IT questions to the Chief Info Security Officer's delegate, governance questions to the Corporate Secretary.
Verify answers are consistent with the schedules (e.g. reinsurance interrogatories versus Schedule F) before sign-off.
Retain the support behind each answer in the workpaper folder.
Obtain Controller review of the full interrogatory set.
checklist.done: interrogatories carry named support, schedule consistency and Controller review.

checklist.step: Run the cross-schedule consistency pack
actions: Run the controlled consistency workbook: state pages to U&I Exhibit, Schedule F to ledger and to reinsurance interrogatories, Schedule P to the ledger and prior statement, Schedule T to state pages.
Clear every check to zero or document the difference with reason and amount — a filed-around difference is an exception, not a note.
Have the Statutory Reporting Manager countersign the completed pack.
File the pack with the schedule workpapers.
checklist.done: the consistency pack is clean or documented and countersigned before filing.

checklist.step: Prepare the crop-specific exhibits for the April 1 RMA package
actions: Build the RMA exhibit set from the filed statement: capacity and surplus evidence, projected premium by state and fund designation, and the maximum reinsurable premium computation per the SRA formula.
Tie each exhibit figure to the filed statement or board-approved plan with page references.
Have the Controller review and the CFO approve the exhibit set.
Deliver to the Regulatory Affairs Manager for the April 1 submission.
checklist.done: the RMA exhibits tie to filed sources with approvals and are delivered for the April 1 package.

checklist.step: File state supplemental schedules by their April 1 deadlines
actions: Work the April 1 supplemental checklist weekly through March: state-specific supplements, actuarial-opinion-related filings and any crop assessment reports.
Submit each through the state's required channel and capture receipts into the evidence log.
Cure any rejection within 3 business days with reviewer re-check.
Close checklist items only on attached evidence.
checklist.done: all April 1 supplements show receipts and any rejection cured inside 3 business days.

checklist.step: Review the complete schedule set page-by-page before filing
actions: Review each schedule against its workpaper, the consistency pack and the prior year for unexplained swings over the review threshold.
Challenge crop-specific presentations: FCIC cession lines, fund-designation splits and state allocations.
Record review notes and clear each before releasing the statement for jurat execution.
Sign the review checklist as the pre-filing gate.
checklist.done: a signed page-by-page review with cleared notes gates the filing.

checklist.step: Handle post-filing corrections on schedules
actions: Log any post-filing error found internally or raised by an analyst, with the schedule, amount and discovery source.
Assess materiality with the Controller: amended filing versus correction in the next statement, documenting the decision.
Resubmit corrected schedules within 3 business days of the decision and capture confirmations.
Feed the error into the close retrospective for template or lineage fixes.
checklist.done: every correction shows a materiality decision, timely resubmission and a retrospective action.

checklist.step: Archive the schedule workpapers with full lineage
actions: Archive per schedule: staged extracts with lineage stamps, workpapers, the consistency pack, review sign-offs and the filed copy.
Label with the 3-year retention period and index by statement year and schedule.
Test that a named schedule's full lineage retrieves within 2 business days.
Record the archive completion to the Controller.
checklist.done: each schedule's lineage archive is complete, labeled, indexed and retrieval-tested.

checklist.step: Update templates for blanks changes before next season
actions: Map the adopted blanks changes for the next statement year to affected schedule templates and software mappings.
Update templates and the consistency workbook under version control with a tested dry run.
Brief preparers on changes at the pre-close meeting with attendance recorded.
File the change log with the procedure.
checklist.done: templates and mappings are updated, dry-run tested and briefed before the first affected close.

checklist.step: Coordinate schedule support for the independent audit
actions: Deliver requested schedule workpapers and lineage to the external auditors through the audit request list.
Track auditor findings touching schedules and route them into the close-issue log.
Confirm audit adjustments that change schedule figures trigger the correction workflow.
Retain the auditor correspondence with the schedule archive.
checklist.done: audit requests are fulfilled from the archive and findings flow into corrections.

checklist.step: Log and remediate schedule exceptions
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each consistency failure filed around, late supplement or material correction, with the amount.
Assign root cause (lineage gap, template error, staffing) and an owner with a date.
Sign closure only after the corrected process is demonstrated in the next cycle.
Carry exceptions into the annual verification test as mandatory retest rows.
checklist.done: every schedule exception is quantified, owned, demonstrated fixed and committed to retest.

testing.step: Build the schedule population from the instructions, not the inventory
actions: Independently list the schedules, interrogatories and supplements required for the statement year from the NAIC instructions and state checklists.
Add the RMA April 1 exhibit set from the SRA and RMA instructions.
Compare to the Company's approved inventory; a required item missing from the inventory is a scope-control fail.
testing.done: an independent required-schedule list exists with inventory omissions logged.

testing.step: Verify filing completeness and timeliness of the set
actions: Trace each required item to its filed copy and confirmation timestamp against March 1 or its April 1 date.
Check correction resubmissions met the 3-business-day standard.
List unfiled or late items as exceptions with day counts.
testing.done: every required item shows timely filing evidence or a quantified exception.

testing.step: Re-perform Schedule F tie-outs and the provision calculation
actions: Independently agree Schedule F ceded premium and recoverables for the FCIC line and 3 sampled private reinsurers to the reinsurance administration system and treaty statements.
Recompute the provision for reinsurance for the sampled reinsurers from aging and security data.
Verify reinsurer status classifications against the domiciliary state's records.
testing.done: Schedule F samples re-tie, the provision recomputes and statuses verify.

testing.step: Re-perform Schedule P consistency on the crop lines
actions: Agree the current diagonal to the ledger and the prior diagonals to last year's filed Schedule P.
Recompute one-year and two-year development for the crop line and compare to the filed figures.
Trace the net-of-FCIC presentation to the cession extract for one accident year.
testing.done: Schedule P crop lines re-agree to ledger, prior statement and cession data.

testing.step: Re-foot the state pages and Schedule T linkage
actions: Re-foot state page totals to the Underwriting & Investment Exhibit and Schedule T to the state pages.
For 5 sampled states, agree state premium to the policy admin allocation extract.
Verify no state shows premium without licensing status supporting it.
testing.done: state allocations re-foot and sampled states trace to source with licensing consistent.

testing.step: Verify the consistency pack ran and differences were genuine
actions: Re-run the consistency workbook on the filed figures and compare results to the countersigned pack.
Investigate any check that passes in the pack but fails on re-run — evidence of manual override.
Verify documented differences carry real explanations with amounts, not placeholders.
testing.done: the pack re-runs to the same results and documented differences withstand challenge.

testing.step: Recompute the RMA exhibit figures
actions: Agree the April 1 exhibit surplus and capacity figures to the filed statement pages cited.
Recompute the maximum reinsurable premium from the SRA formula inputs.
Verify CFO approval pre-dates the RMA transmission.
testing.done: RMA exhibits recompute and tie to cited sources with the approval sequence intact.

testing.step: Verify lineage archives support the filed figures
actions: For 3 sampled schedules, retrieve the archive and walk source extract → workpaper → filed line without preparer assistance.
Check lineage stamps (run date, query, record count) exist on each extract used.
Time the retrieval against the 2-business-day standard.
testing.done: sampled schedules walk from source to filed line on archived evidence alone, on time.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with schedule, amount and defect type.
Assign root cause (lineage gap, override, template error, scope miss) and an accountable owner with a date.
Require Controller sign-off on closure with the fix demonstrated in the next cycle.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception is quantified, owned, dated and closure-gated on a demonstrated fix.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — against the tie-out, timeliness and consistency thresholds.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared none of the tested schedules, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Controller and Audit Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Appoint the independent auditor and confirm eligibility

Obtain the firm's written independence confirmation covering the crop writing company and affiliates.
Take the appointment to the Audit Committee for approval and minute it.
File the state's required auditor-registration or awareness letter with the domiciliary regulator within the rule's window after appointment.
checklist.done: an approved, independent auditor is appointed with rotation checked and the awareness letter filed.

checklist.step: Plan the engagement with crop-specific audit areas on the table
actions: Hold the planning meeting covering the crop risk areas: FCIC cession accounting and the escrow/settlement cycle, fund-designation splits, SSAP 78 treatments, Schedule F presentation and the RMA data reconciliations.
Agree materiality, timing and the deliverables list working back from the June 1 filing date.
Introduce the auditors to the Statutory Reporting Manager, Reinsurance Accountant and Reserving Actuary as area contacts.
Document the agreed plan and circulate to area owners.
checklist.done: a documented engagement plan names crop risk areas, contacts and a June 1-backed timeline.

checklist.step: Build and load the PBC list with owners and dates
actions: Load every PBC item into AuditBoard with description, owner, due date and the audit area it supports.
Sequence items so trial balance, reconciliations and cession support land before fieldwork start.
Configure due-date alerts and the 5-day-late escalation to the CFO.
Baseline the list so scope additions are visible as changes.
checklist.done: the complete PBC list is loaded, sequenced, alerted and baselined in AuditBoard.

checklist.step: Deliver PBC evidence on time and track completion
actions: Deliver each item through AuditBoard with the preparer's sign-off, keeping the delivered version immutable.
Chase owners at T-3 days and report weekly on-time statistics to the Controller.
Log auditor follow-up requests as child items so nothing lives in email alone.
Escalate any item 5 days late to the CFO with the blocker named.
checklist.done: PBC delivery runs at or above 90% on-time with late items escalated and follow-ups tracked.

checklist.step: Support fieldwork over the FCIC cession and escrow cycle
actions: Walk the auditors through the FCIC cession accounting: weekly transaction-cutoff data flow, escrow settlements, and the underwriting-gain/loss sharing calculation under the SRA formula.
Provide the reconciliation of ledger cession balances to RMA settlement activity with dispositioned differences.
Respond to sample selections over ceded balances within the agreed turnaround.
Log auditor observations on the cession area for the finding process.
checklist.done: the cession walkthrough, reconciliation and samples are delivered and observations logged.

checklist.step: Coordinate the reserve audit with the actuaries
actions: Provide the crop reserve analysis, triangles and the Appointed Actuary's opinion workpapers to the auditor's actuarial specialists.
Reconcile the reserve data to Schedule P and the ledger before handover.
Attend the actuarial challenge sessions and document range discussions and conclusions.
Track any reserve adjustment through the close-adjustment workflow with Controller approval.
checklist.done: reserve support reconciles to filed data and challenge-session conclusions are documented.

checklist.step: Manage audit adjustments and the passed-adjustment summary
actions: Record agreed audit adjustments through controlled top-side entries with support attached.
Review the schedule of passed (unrecorded) adjustments and document the immateriality rationale for each.
Confirm adjusted figures flow through to the audited statutory statements and any affected schedules.
Present adjustments and passed items to the Audit Committee.
checklist.done: all adjustments are recorded or documented as passed with rationale, and presented to the committee.

checklist.step: Review the draft audited statements and opinion
actions: Compare the draft audited statements to the filed annual statement and reconcile any differences (audit adjustments, reclassifications) with a bridging schedule.
Review the opinion language and notes, including the SSAP 78 crop program disclosures and reinsurance notes covering the FCIC arrangement.
Route the draft to the Controller and CFO for review comments on a tracked list.
Confirm the auditors clear every comment before finalization.
checklist.done: the draft reconciles to the filed statement via a bridging schedule and all comments are cleared.

checklist.step: Sign the management representation letter and finalize

Sign dated as of the opinion date.
Receive the final signed opinion and audited statements from the firm.
Minute the Audit Committee's acceptance of the final report.
checklist.done: a signed representation letter, final opinion and committee acceptance are on file.

checklist.step: File the audited financials by June 1
actions: File the audited statutory financial statements with the domiciliary state by June 1 through the state's required channel, and with other states requiring copies per their checklists.
Capture filing receipts into the evidence log the same day.
Confirm any required communication of internal-control findings accompanies the filing per the Model Audit Rule.
Cure any filing rejection within 3 business days.
checklist.done: the June 1 filing shows same-day receipts in every required state with rejections cured in 3 business days.

checklist.step: Furnish the audited financials to RMA
actions: Deliver the audited financial statements to RMA per the Plan of Operations instructions — as a supplement to the April 1 package where the audit completes later, with a transmittal referencing the AIP and reinsurance year.
Retain proof of transmission and RMA's acknowledgement.
Answer RMA follow-up questions on the audited figures within 45 days of each FCIC request.
Log the correspondence in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: RMA holds the audited statements with transmission proof and follow-ups answered inside 45 days.

checklist.step: Work the management letter into owned remediation plans

Assign an owner and a remediation date per finding; the CFO signs each plan.
Track progress monthly and test the fix before closure — closure on assertion alone is not permitted.
Report status to the Audit Committee quarterly until all findings close.
checklist.done: every finding carries a CFO-signed plan, monthly tracking and a tested closure.

checklist.step: Handle a material weakness or qualified opinion as a regulatory event

Document every notification decision with General Counsel.
checklist.done: any adverse outcome shows timely regulator notifications, an RMA impact decision and an owned program.

Apply the 3-year retention label and test retrieval within 2 business days.
Log any FCIC/RMA artifact request and its fulfillment date against the 45-day target.
checklist.done: the indexed artifact set retrieves on time and FCIC requests are logged with fulfillment dates.

Assign root cause and an owner with a date; the CFO signs closure.
Hold the post-audit debrief with the Statutory Reporting Manager and area owners, feeding process fixes into the close procedure and confirming next year's rotation position and engagement timing.
Verify repeat findings from the prior management letter are flagged for escalated treatment.
Carry exceptions into the annual verification test as mandatory retest rows.
checklist.done: every cycle exception is quantified, owned, CFO-signed and committed to retest, with the debrief filed.

Confirm the domiciliary state's current rule text for the year's deadlines rather than relying on last year's memo.
testing.done: a complete cycle record set is assembled against the current rule text.

testing.step: Verify auditor eligibility and appointment governance
actions: Check the lead partner's rotation history against the five-year limit using engagement records.
Verify the written independence confirmation covers the writing company and affiliates for the audit period.
Trace the Audit Committee approval minute and the awareness-letter filing date against the rule's window.
testing.done: rotation, independence and appointment governance verify against source records.

testing.step: Recompute the filing timeline against June 1
actions: Trace the audited-financials filing receipts for the domiciliary state and each copy state against June 1.
Verify the RMA transmittal and acknowledgement for the audited statements.
Recompute response intervals for any FCIC follow-up against the 45-day target.
testing.done: all filings and RMA deliveries show timestamps inside their deadlines or quantified misses.

testing.step: Reconcile audited statements to the filed annual statement

Confirm recorded adjustments posted through controlled top-side entries with support.
Check passed adjustments carry documented immateriality rationale and committee presentation.
testing.done: the bridge re-walks completely with every difference supported and governed.

testing.step: Verify PBC process health
actions: Compute the on-time PBC delivery rate from AuditBoard history against the 90% standard.
Verify 5-day-late escalations fired to the CFO where triggered.
Check delivered versions were immutable and follow-ups were tracked as child items, not email threads.
testing.done: PBC statistics, escalations and version control verify from system history.

testing.step: Trace management-letter findings to tested closures
actions: Trace every finding to a CFO-signed remediation plan, monthly tracking entries and closure evidence showing the fix was tested.
Flag closures made on assertion without test evidence as exceptions.
Compare against the prior year's letter and mark any repeat finding — repeats are automatic fails of the remediation control.
testing.done: every finding shows a signed plan and tested closure, with repeats identified.

testing.step: Verify crop-specific audit coverage
actions: Read the engagement plan and confirm the FCIC cession, escrow settlement, fund-designation and SSAP 78 areas were in scope.
Verify the cession reconciliation to RMA settlement activity was provided and examined.
Confirm reserve challenge sessions occurred with documented conclusions consistent with the opinion.
testing.done: crop risk areas verifiably received audit coverage with documented outcomes.

testing.step: Test FCIC artifact-production readiness
actions: Request the full artifact package for the year through the index and time retrieval against the 2-business-day standard.
Verify the cross-index to internal audit reports on Protected Information systems exists, per the SRA's reach to internal audits.
Trace any actual FCIC/RMA artifact request to a fulfillment date inside 45 days.
testing.done: the package retrieves on time, cross-indexed, with real requests fulfilled inside 45 days.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception — filing miss, untested closure, repeat finding, artifact-production failure — with the day count or defect quantified.
Assign root cause and an accountable owner with a date; the CFO signs closure.
Confirm any regulator or RMA notification obligations arising from exceptions were assessed with General Counsel.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception is quantified, owned, dated and notification-assessed.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — against the June 1, remediation and 45-day-production thresholds.
Sign the workpaper as the independent reviewer, having neither prepared audited balances nor coordinated the engagement.
Report to the Audit Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the Audit Committee.
